articles.fullText:
The China Film Showcase was held on Tuesday at the Stella Cinema in Dublin, Ireland, bringing together more than 200 guests and moviegoers.
Attendees included Jiang Haiqing, a member of China Media Group's (CMG) editorial board and chairman of China International Television Corporation (CITVC); Zhao Yingguang, chargé d'affaires ad interim of the Chinese Embassy in Ireland; former Irish Prime Minister Enda Kenny; former Irish Ambassador to China Declan Kelleher; former European Parliament President Pat Cox; John Kennedy, principal officer at Ireland's Department of Culture, Communications and Sport; Liang Hong, director of CMG's Film, Drama and Documentary Center; Dublin City Councillor Danny Byrne; and Anthony Leo, CEO of animation studio Cartoon Saloon.
Jiang Haiqing, a member of CMG's editorial board and chairman of CITVC, addresses the launch event in Dublin, Ireland, November 10, 2026. /CMG
Jiang noted that CMG has long been committed to promoting innovation in the film industry and international exchange.
She expressed hope that the screenings would give Irish audiences a better understanding of contemporary Chinese cinema and help strengthen cultural ties between the two countries.
John Kennedy, principal officer at Ireland's Department of Culture, Communications and Sport, addresses the launch event in Dublin, Ireland, November 10, 2026. /CMG
Kennedy said film serves as an important bridge across languages and national borders, fostering mutual understanding and strengthening bilateral relations.
He expressed hope for closer cooperation between the film industries of China and Ireland.
Liang Hong, director of CMG's Film, Drama and Documentary Center, at the launch event in Dublin, Ireland, November 10, 2026. /CMG
As part of the showcase, a special screening of CMG's documentary Blue Planet Outside the Window, also known as Shenzhou 13, was held followed by a discussion.
The film features 8K footage of Earth captured from orbit, offering a perspective on the planet from space. The cinema quickly filled to capacity, with additional seats added to accommodate the audience.
Liang thanked Irish audiences for their warm response and announced that the documentary had won the Best Documentary/Science and Education Film award at the China Golden Rooster Awards.
She said documentaries can transcend national borders and bring people closer through shared emotions, adding that CMG hopes to explore joint documentary projects with Irish counterparts.
The showcase also featured two other CMG productions, the documentary Fabric of Lives and the animated film The Reunion Journey. Together, the three films showcased the diversity of themes and artistic styles in contemporary Chinese filmmaking.

articles.fullText:
Somalia has ordered the United Arab Emirates (UAE) ambassador to leave the country within 72 hours and recalled its own envoy from Abu Dhabi, accusing the Gulf state of violating its sovereignty.
Information Minister Abdifatah Kasim Mohamud announced the decision on Thursday, warning that action would be taken against anyone cooperating with the UAE in what he described as an "open invasion" of Somalia.
The minister did not specify the alleged violations. However, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud accused the UAE in a speech on Tuesday of providing economic and political support to some regional Somali administrations in opposition to the federal government.
The UAE foreign ministry had not immediately commented on the latest developments.
The latest move follows Somalia's decision in January to terminate all agreements with the UAE, including port deals and defense and security cooperation, accusing Abu Dhabi of undermining its sovereignty.
Three self-governing Somali regions with close ties to the UAE rejected the federal government's decision at the time.
The UAE has expanded its economic, military and diplomatic presence across the Horn of Africa, including through investments in ports and military infrastructure along key international shipping routes.
Relations have also been shaped by tensions over the distribution of power within Somalia. The federal government has struggled to extend its authority across the country and defeat Islamist militants despite years of international support, including African peacekeeping operations and US air strikes.
The UAE trained hundreds of Somali troops between 2014 and 2018. It also continues to pay salaries and provide logistical support to around 3,400 military police and special forces personnel in and around the capital, according to senior Somali sources.
Beyond its military involvement, the UAE has established direct ties with regional Somali administrations, investing hundreds of millions of dollars in ports and military infrastructure along the country's coast.

articles.fullText:
Chinese President Xi Jinping's speech at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on Thursday has drawn widespread support from attendees, who stressed the importance of Asia-Pacific cooperation and welcomed his vision as offering clear direction for the region's future development.
Gong Xiaofeng, director of the Shenzhen University APEC Research Institute, said President Xi's speech offered strategic insights amid the changing global landscape and put forward a clear vision for building an Asia-Pacific community characterized by solidarity, openness, innovation and inclusive development.
Gong also highlighted the transformation of China's role as Xi's vision reflects China's evolution from an active participant in Asia-Pacific cooperation to a leading force in shaping its future, demonstrating how high-level strategic thinking can be translated into practical action.
Tahir Farooq, the chief editor of Daily Ittehad, also underscores the significance of Asia-Pacific as a crucial region of cooperation, and said this year's APEC meeting carries special significance and hope it will deliver more tangible, practical outcomes.
Speaking of the specific aspects in which APEC economies can come together in cooperation, Xu Yangsheng, President of the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, emphasized the need to foster an open and innovative ecosystem and promote the widespread application of artificial intelligence (AI).
Xu also pointed out the advantage of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area as an ideal hub for innovation, which is capable of continuously generating technological breakthroughs to support the AI industry.

articles.fullText:
(ECNS) -- China has introduced its first system for evaluating artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities in vehicle cockpits, as automakers increasingly turn to AI to enhance the in-car experience.
The system, developed by the China Automotive Technology and Research Center (CATARC), rates cockpit AI capabilities on a five-level scale from C1 to C5. It aims to translate users' subjective experiences into measurable indicators, covering eight core capabilities and behavioral attributes across nine driving scenarios.
Zhang Yanan, deputy general manager of CATARC Intelligent Technology, said the framework assesses capabilities such as perception, execution, autonomy and evolution in scenarios involving smart mobility, emotional companionship and health care.
The system also records these assessments in a structured database to better reflect real-world driving conditions, Zhang said. The center has completed an initial round of validation tests using the framework, which is intended to provide consumers with an objective benchmark for comparing AI capabilities across vehicles.
According to CATARC, more than 90% of domestically produced new energy vehicles priced above 200,000 yuan (about $28,200) now offer AI-powered cockpit features that generate more than 30 million in-car interactions a day.
China's intelligent cockpit market is expected to exceed 180 billion yuan (about $26.98 billion) in 2026, with smart cockpit features playing an increasingly important role in car-buying decisions.

articles.fullText:
More than four decades ago, Shenzhen was a quiet fishing village. Today, drones deliver meals through the air, robots patrol its streets and cutting-edge technology is part of everyday life. A global hub for innovation and talent, the city is now set to host the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting.
So, what powers this remarkable transformation?
CGTN reporter Li Jingjing teams up with US vlogger Cyrus Janssen, who has more than two million followers, to explore the city and discover the forces behind its remarkable rise.
In Shenzhen, ideas can move from concept to product at remarkable speed. With design, prototyping and manufacturing resources closely connected, and the Greater Bay Area providing an integrated network of industrial support, entrepreneurs can get the key steps in place in just over a week. That's “Shenzhen speed.”
Having spent time in China over the past 20 years, Janssen has witnessed firsthand the country's remarkable progress, particularly how infrastructure development has improved people's lives across the country. His message to the world: Look beyond media narratives, come to China, meet its people and see the country for yourself.
articles.fullTextCn:
四十多年前，深圳还是一个宁静的渔村。如今，无人机在空中送餐，机器人在街道上巡逻，尖端技术已成为日常生活的一部分。作为全球创新和人才中心，这座城市现在将主办第33届亚太经合组织（APEC）经济领导人会议。那么，是什么推动了这一非凡的转变？CGTN记者李晶晶与美国视频博主Cyrus Janssen（拥有超过200万粉丝）联手探索这座城市，揭示其非凡崛起背后的力量。在深圳，想法可以以惊人的速度从概念变为产品。由于设计、原型制作和制造资源紧密相连，加上大湾区提供了一体化的产业支持网络，企业家可以在短短一周多的时间内完成关键步骤。这就是“深圳速度”。

在过去的20年里，Janssen在中国度过了一段时间，他亲眼目睹了中国的显著进步，特别是基础设施建设如何改善了全国各地人民的生活。他向世界传达的信息是：超越媒体叙事，来中国，结识这里的人民，亲自看看这个国家。
